This work showcases Fazil's dual talent as both the director and screenwriter, contributing to its resonance within Indian cinema.

Heartbreakers, directed by David Mirkin, is a comedy film released on May 24, 2001. This entertaining movie features a talented cast, including Sigourney Weaver, Jason Lee, Zach Galifianakis, and Carrie Fisher. Produced by Winchester Films, Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, and Davis Entertainment, it was filmed in Long Beach. With a production budget of $35 million, the film dives into themes of deception and romance, showcasing the antics of a con artist mother-daughter duo.

Seoul Jesus, a notable drama film directed by Jang Seon-u, was released in South Korea on January 1, 1986. Featuring Kim Myung-gon in a significant role, this South Korean production delves into themes that resonate with audiences even today.
Closing Numbers, directed by Stephen Whittaker, was released in 1993. This British film explores themes relevant to its time and showcases the distinctive style of its talented director.

Ride a Violent Mile, directed by Charles Marquis Warren, is a Western film that was released in the United States on January 1, 1957. Featuring John Agar in a prominent role, this cinematic piece transports audiences to the rugged terrain of the American West. The film explores themes typical of its genre, showcasing the struggles of its characters against a backdrop of frontier challenges.

Separation is a notable British film directed by Jack Bond that premiered on January 1, 1968. Featuring the talented Jane Arden, this cinematic work explores complex themes and showcases the creative vision of its director. Set against the backdrop of the United Kingdom, it remains a significant entry in the history of film during that era.

Released in January 1994, this Indian action film, Athiradi Padai, showcases the directorial skills of R.K. Selvamani. The film features a notable cast, including Suman and Rahman, who contribute significantly to the story's excitement and intensity.

Wake, directed by Henry LeRoy Finch, is a captivating film that was released in the United States on January 1, 2003. This American production features notable performances from actors Martin Landau and Gale Harold, who bring depth to their characters, contributing to the movie's emotional resonance. With its unique storytelling, Wake stands out in the early 2000s film landscape.

Released in 1957, Badlands of Montana is a Western film directed by Daniel B. Ullman. This American production takes viewers on a journey through the rugged landscapes of the West, showcasing the themes typical of the genre. With its historical context and captivating storytelling, the film remains a notable entry in the Western canon.

Delirios de amor is a Spanish film that was released on January 1, 1986. This romantic drama captures the essence of love and longing, showcasing the unique storytelling style that Spanish cinema is known for.

Web of Passion, a drama film released in January 1959, showcases the directorial talents of Claude Chabrol. This French film features notable performances from Madeleine Robinson and Chabrol himself, who also contributed as the screenwriter. The movie weaves a compelling narrative that reflects Chabrol's unique style, hinting at the intricacies of human relationships.

In a different context, Philippe de Broca is another prominent director known for his engaging storytelling, although he was not involved in the making of this particular film. With its dramatic themes and strong character development, Web of Passion remains a noteworthy entry in Chabrol’s filmography.

Vetri Kodi Kattu is a 2000 Indian film directed and written by Cheran, showcasing a blend of drama and emotional depth. This soundtrack-driven movie features Murali as a key cast member, contributing to its engaging narrative. Released on June 30, 2000, it remains a notable work in the realm of Indian cinema.

Apache Warrior is a Western film directed by Elmo Williams that was released in the United States in January 1957. The story features Keith Larsen in a prominent role, contributing to the film's engaging portrayal of the genre. Set against the backdrop of the American West, this classic film blends action and drama, showcasing the cinematic style of its time.

Snowboard Academy is a comedy directed by John Shepphird, highlighting a unique blend of humor and winter sports. The film features a diverse cast, including Jim Varney, Polly Shannon, and Brigitte Nielsen, all of whom bring their comedic talents to the story set in the United States. With its American roots, the film has carved out a niche for itself in the realm of lighthearted sports comedies.

Durak is a gripping thriller film from Turkey, featuring notable performances by Emre Altuğ and Bedük. With its intense narrative, this production showcases the talents of its compelling cast while captivating audiences with suspenseful storytelling.

K. S. Ravi directed the action film Honest Raj, released on January 1, 1994. The film features Vijayakanth in a leading role and showcases a gripping storyline typical of the genre. With K. S. Ravi also penning the screenplay, the film combines his vision both behind and in front of the camera.

Spoilers of the Forest is a 1957 drama and Western film directed by Joseph Kane. This American production features Rod Cameron in a leading role and was written by Bruce Manning. Produced by Republic Pictures, the film showcases a compelling narrative set against the backdrop of the American West.

Jellyfish is a poignant drama film directed by Etgar Keret, who also stars in the project. This Israeli film, released on March 13, 2008, seamlessly blends elements of hyperlink cinema to create a unique storytelling experience. In addition to Keret, Gideon Levy is part of the ensemble cast, contributing to the film's rich narrative. The intertwining lives depicted in Jellyfish offer a reflective glimpse into the human condition through its multifaceted characters.

Geçmiş is a Turkish film directed by Çagdas Çagri that was released on July 14, 2017. The movie explores themes deeply rooted in Turkish culture and showcases the director's unique perspective on the subject matter.

Snowboarďáci, directed by Karel Janák, is a notable entry in the sport film genre that showcases the excitement of snowboarding. The film features prominent performances by Otakar Brousek Jr. and Pavel Nový, both of whom bring their characters to life in this thrilling winter sports adventure. With its engaging storyline and dynamic visuals, this cinematic piece captures the spirit of competition and camaraderie among snowboarders.

Outlaw Queen is a Western film directed by Herbert S. Greene. Released on January 1, 1957, this American production offers a classic take on the genre, featuring the typical themes of outlaws and frontier justice. Set against the backdrop of the American West, it captures the essence of its time while showcasing Greene's directorial style.

Thrill, a detective film released in January 1941, showcases the collaborative talent of its director, Giacomo Gentilomo, and screenwriters Alessandro De Stefani and Mario Monicelli. This Italian production features a notable cast, including Clara Calamai and Carlo Campanini, who bring depth to the intricate plot. The film stands out not only for its engaging storyline but also for the craftsmanship involved in bringing the characters to life.

Untouchable, directed and written by Kristin Hansen, is a poignant comedy-drama centered around the world of physiotherapy. Released on June 1, 2011, this American film features a talented cast, including Teresa Huang, Kelly Marie Tran, Anthony Cannata, and Lisa Winans. The storyline explores the challenges and humorous moments experienced by physiotherapists and their patients, depicting both the comedic and heartfelt aspects of their interactions.

Snowbound, directed by David MacDonald, is an adventure film that transports viewers to the breathtaking Alps. Released on January 1, 1948, this British production by Gainsborough Pictures features a captivating performance by Dennis Price. While the narrative unfolds largely in the stunning mountain backdrop, it is rooted in London, adding layers to the storyline.

Who Killed Bambi? is a Spanish film directed by Santiago Amodeo. This intriguing story features a talented cast, including Clara Lago, Quim Gutiérrez, and José Ángel Egido, who bring depth to the narrative. Set against the vibrant backdrop of Spain, the movie combines humor with drama, showcasing the distinct style of its director.

Broadway is a musical film directed by Paul Fejos, featuring a standout performance by Evelyn Brent. Set in the bustling heart of New York City, this cinematic piece showcases the vibrant atmosphere of the city through its engaging storyline crafted by screenwriter George Abbott. The film beautifully blends music and narrative, making it a notable entry in the genre of musical cinema.

The Earth and the Sky is a drama film directed by Manuel Octavio Gómez, who also wrote the screenplay for this poignant story. Released in January 1976, this Cuban film features notable performances from Martha Jean-Claude and Samuel Claxton. The film delves into themes that resonate deeply within the socio-political context of its time.

Snowbound, directed by Ruben Preuss, is a gripping thriller film released in 2001. This American production features a talented cast including Erika Eleniak, Monika Schnarre, and Peter Dobson, who each bring suspenseful dynamics to the storyline. Set against a chilling backdrop, the film invites viewers into a world of tension and intrigue.

Dance Academy is a film that was released on January 1, 1988. This Australian production takes viewers into the intense world of dance and the challenges faced by aspiring performers. Its exploration of ambition and artistry resonates even today, making it a noteworthy addition to the dance genre.

Bullwhip, a film released on January 1, 1958, was directed by Harmon Jones. This American production features notable performances by James Griffith and Hank Worden, who both play significant roles in the story. The film stands out in its genre and reflects the cinematic style of the late 1950s in the United States.

Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade is an adventure film directed by Steven Spielberg. Set in various locations, including Berlin, the story follows the iconic archaeologist Indiana Jones along with his father, Henry Jones. The screenplay was crafted by Menno Meyjes, adding depth to the thrilling narrative that has captivated audiences since its release.

Carl Boese directed The Trip to Youth, a captivating exploration of coming-of-age themes that resonates across generations. This film stands out for its poignant storytelling and has garnered appreciation from audiences for its insightful portrayal of youth and the journey to self-discovery.

The 10 Commandments of Chloe, directed by Princeton Holt, is a gripping drama film from the United States that was released on January 1, 2012. Jason Burkey features in the cast, contributing to the film's compelling narrative and character development. This production showcases the intricacies of human relationships, making it a notable entry in the genre.
Broadway Gondolier, directed by Lloyd Bacon, was released on January 1, 1935. In this charming film, Dick Powell delivers a memorable performance that captivates audiences with his talent.

Snowstorm, directed and written by Antun Vrdoljak, is a drama film that was released in 1977. The film showcases the complex emotions and narratives typical of Vrdoljak's storytelling style, making it a notable work in the landscape of drama cinema from that era.
Sexual Roulette, a film directed by Gary Graver, was released in January 1996. This American production explores themes of desire and intrigue, showcasing Graver's distinctive filmmaking style.

Wilhelm Furtwängler - Longing for Germany, a documentary released on January 1, 2003, explores the life and legacy of the renowned conductor. This film delves into Furtwängler's complex relationship with Germany during a tumultuous period in history.

Diary of a Lost Woman, directed and written by Richard Oswald, is a silent drama film that was released in Germany in 1918. This poignant work explores deep emotional themes, characteristic of Oswald's storytelling style during the silent film era.

Suite 16 is a film directed by Dominique Deruddere and features a talented cast that includes Géraldine Pailhas, Antonie Kamerling, and Viviane De Muynck. The screenplay was crafted by Lise Mayer and Charlie Higson, adding to the film's unique storytelling.

Released in January 2005, the horror film Snuff-Movie, directed by Bernard Rose, showcases a chilling narrative that reflects its title. Set in the United Kingdom, this unsettling piece of cinema was produced by Capitol Films. 

The cast features notable performances from Jeroen Krabbé, Lyndsey Marshal, Teri Harrison, and Alastair Mackenzie, each contributing to the eerie atmosphere that defines this British production. As the story unfolds, the film explores dark themes that have drawn both intrigue and controversy among viewers.

The Mill, directed by Mohan Dayaram Bhavnani, is a notable Indian film released on January 1, 1934. This early cinematic work reflects the artistic style and cultural context of India during that period.

Amici per la pelle is an Italian film directed by Franco Rossi, set against the vibrant backdrop of Rome. The cast features notable performances from Marcella Rovena, Ignazio Leone, and Günter Lüdke. The screenplay was penned by Leonardo Benvenuti, adding depth to the narrative. This captivating story showcases the talents of its diverse actors while immersing viewers in the rich culture of Italy's capital city.

Tuđa zemlja, a drama film directed by Jože Gale, was released on February 16, 1957. This poignant movie features a notable cast, including Rade Marković, Ilija Džuvalekovski, and Vlastimir Đuza Stojiljković, who deliver compelling performances that enhance the emotional depth of the story.

Directed by Terra Shin, this engaging action film seamlessly blends elements of a spy thriller. Written by Chun Sung-Il, the film also showcases performances from Jang Young-nam and Kang Sin-il, contributing to its dynamic storytelling. Snuff Bottle Connection is a martial arts film directed by both Liu Li-Li and Chin-Hu Tung. Featuring the talented Hwang Jang-lee, this action-packed movie showcases impressive fight choreography and a gripping storyline that martial arts enthusiasts are sure to enjoy.

Brasserie Romantiek, directed by Joël Vanhoebrouck, is a charming film from Belgium that showcases the talents of Mathijs Scheepers and Sara De Roo. The screenplay for this delightful story was crafted by Jean-Claude van Rijckeghem, adding depth to the narrative.

Zle pare is a comedy film that was released on July 16, 1956. This classic features a talented cast, including actors Veljko Mandić, Antun Nalis, Karlo Bulić, and Đorđe Milaković, all of whom contribute to the film's humorous narrative. The screenplay for this entertaining Brazilian film was penned by Ratko Đurović, adding a distinctive voice to its comedic elements.

Amici più di prima, a comedy film released on January 1, 1976, showcases the talents of several notable actors including Ciccio Ingrassia, Andrea Bosic, and Paolo Carlini. The film is directed by a trio of filmmakers: Marino Girolami, Giorgio Simonelli, and Giovanni Grimaldi, bringing diverse visions to this humorous narrative. 

Set in the vibrant style of the mid-1970s, this Italian production is marked by its ensemble cast and comedic elements, which continue to resonate with fans of the genre.

Snowfire is a Western film that was released on January 1, 1958. Directed by Dorrell McGowan and Stuart E. McGowan, this American production features Don Megowan in the lead role. Set against the backdrop of the American frontier, the film captures the spirit of classic Westerns while showcasing the talents of its well-known cast.

Male stvari is a drama film directed by Boško Kosanović that was released on January 1, 1957. The narrative features talented actors, including Janez Vrhovec and Tomislav Tanhofer, who contribute to the film's compelling portrayal of its themes.

Snushanerne is a 1936 comedy film directed by Lau Lauritzen, who also penned the screenplay alongside Alice O'Fredericks. This charming Danish production features Asbjørn Andersen in its cast, bringing to life the humor and wit characteristic of the era.

Amleto di Carmelo Bene (da Shakespeare a Laforgue) is a 1974 comedy-drama directed and written by Carmelo Bene himself. This Italian film showcases an impressive cast including Laura Morante, Susanna Javicoli, Carmelo Bene, Alfiero Vincenti, and Cosimo Cinieri.

Set against a backdrop that blends Shakespearean themes with a unique vision, this film reflects the creative spirit of its creator. With its theatrical roots and a distinctive style, Amleto di Carmelo Bene invites viewers into a world where drama and comedy intertwine seamlessly.

Directed by Viktor Tauš and written by Radek John, this film was released on January 1, 2008, and represents a collaboration between the Czech Republic and Slovakia. So's Your Aunt Emma is a 1942 comedy film directed by Jean Yarbrough. This American production showcases the humor of its time, presenting a light-hearted narrative that has entertained audiences for decades.

Andrzej Wajda directed Canal, a poignant portrayal of the harrowing experiences during World War II. Released on April 20, 1957, it captures the trials of soldiers navigating the perils of war. The film's impact continued to resonate, leading to further releases, including one on January 8, 1959, and another that debuted at the beginning of 1957. With its stark representation of conflict, Canal remains a significant work in the canon of war cinema.

U našeg Martina is a film directed by Branko Majer, who skillfully brings the story to life with his unique vision. The cast includes talented actors such as Janez Vrhovec and Boris Buzančić, both of whom deliver compelling performances that enhance the film's emotional depth.

Hum Paanch is an Indian film directed by Bapu that seamlessly blends elements of action, family, and drama. The ensemble cast includes renowned actors such as Sanjeev Kumar, Amrish Puri, Naseeruddin Shah, Mithun Chakraborty, and Shabana Azmi, all of whom deliver memorable performances.

Written by Mullapudi Venkata Ramana, this captivating story showcases the complexities of family dynamics within an action-packed narrative. The film has garnered attention not only for its engaging plot but also for the stellar performances from its talented cast.

Kentervilski duh, a drama film directed by Sava Mrmak, was released on January 1, 1962. Coffee, adds depth and emotion to this United States production, making it a memorable entry in classic cinema.

Perfect Strangers, directed by Bretaigne Windust, skillfully blends elements of comedy and drama within the framework of a trial film. Produced by Warner Bros., this engaging story captivates audiences with its sharp wit and compelling narrative.

Sun Sajna is a 1982 Indian film directed by Chander H. Bahl. The cast features notable actors such as Mithun Chakraborty, Iftekhar, and Jagdeep, as well as Ram Mohan and Ranjeeta Kaur. Shari Springer Berman directed the biographical film American Splendor, which premiered on January 20, 2003. The movie is based on the graphic novel American Splendor and the memoir Our Cancer Year, highlighting the life of comic book writer Harvey Pekar.

Recognized for its artistic merit, American Splendor received the Sundance Film Festival U.S. Dramatic Grand Jury Prize and was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Writing, Adapted Screenplay. Produced by Good Machine, this film uniquely blends drama with elements of reality, offering an engaging portrait of a complex figure in American culture.

Ratra Aarambh is an Indian film that was released on January 1, 1999. Among its notable cast members is Dilip Prabhavalkar, who brings his talent to this engaging story.

I fobici, a comedy film released on January 1, 1999, features an engaging screenplay crafted by Giancarlo Scarchilli and Giovanni Veronesi. Directed by Scarchilli and produced by Medusa Film, this lighthearted movie boasts a talented cast that includes Riccardo Garrone, Sabrina Ferilli, and Daniele Liotti.

A Better Life is a drama film directed by Chris Weitz, which premiered in the United States on January 1, 2011. Set primarily in Los Angeles, this poignant story explores the struggles of a Mexican immigrant who dreams of a better future for his son amidst the challenges of his new life.

Filmed in São Paulo, the movie features notable performances from actors such as Joaquín Cosio Osuna and Nancy Lenehan. Produced by Summit Entertainment, A Better Life gained recognition for its heartfelt narrative and social commentary, later making its way to theaters on June 24, 2011.

No Questions Asked is a compelling crime film that blends elements of film noir and LGBT themes, showcasing the unique narrative style prevalent in 1950s cinema. Directed by Harold F. Kress, this American production features a talented cast, including Jean Hagen, Arlene Dahl, and Robert J. Wilke. 

The screenplay, written by Sidney Sheldon, encapsulates the complexities of its characters within a gripping storyline. In addition to the prominent actors, Juanita Moore and Bess Flowers contribute to the film's rich ensemble, further enhancing its depth. Released on January 1, 1951, this film marked a significant moment in cinema history.

Rats in the Ranks is an Australian documentary film directed by both Bob Connolly and Robin Anderson. Released on January 1, 1996, this insightful film explores the complexities of local politics and the dynamics within a small community. Using a unique blend of candid interviews and real-life events, the documentary provides a thought-provoking look at governance and public engagement in Australia.

Shadow in the Sky is a drama film directed by Fred M. Wilcox, which features a noteworthy performance by Ralph Meeker. Released on July 18, 1952, this American film explores its themes with depth and sensitivity. Set against a backdrop reflective of its time, it pushes the boundaries of the genre and showcases the talents of its cast.

Directed by M. Sadiq, the Brazilian film Rattan showcases the talents of screenwriter D. N. Madhok. Released on January 1, 1944, it features notable performances from Swaran Lata, who plays a significant role in the story. This classic movie is remembered for its engaging narrative and strong character development.

The Castiglioni Brothers, a film directed by Corrado D'Errico, was released in Italy on January 1, 1937. This Italian film features a notable cast that includes Luisa Ferida, Silvio Bagolini, and Camillo Pilotto, each contributing to the film's unique charm and appeal.

Las adolescentes is a Spanish drama film directed by Pedro Masó and produced by Impala. This work features a talented cast, including Eduardo Fajardo, Cristina Galbó, and Maria Perschy, all contributing to the film's emotional depth. The screenplay was penned by Santiago Moncada Mercadal, adding to the overall quality of this poignant narrative.

Rattlers is a horror film directed by John McCauley that was released in the United States in 1976. This chilling story features performances by cast members Darwin Joston and Eric Lawson, who contribute to the film's tense atmosphere. As an embodiment of '70s horror, it explores themes of nature's terror, specifically through the eyes of those encountering deadly rattlesnakes.

Once a Thief is a 1950 film noir and dramatic tale directed by W. Lee Wilder. Set in the United States, the film features a notable performance by Cesar Romero, who plays a compelling role in this cinematic exploration of crime and morality. Released on July 7, 1950, the film combines the tension of film noir with the emotional depth of drama, making it a noteworthy entry in the genre during that era.

I fuorilegge is a detective film directed by Aldo Vergano, who also contributed to the screenplay alongside fellow writers Giuseppe Mangione, Gian Paolo Callegari, and Sergio Pugliese. Set in Italy, this intriguing movie features a notable cast, including Vittorio Gassman, Attilio Dottesio, Leonardo De Mitri, and Umberto Spadaro. 

The film intertwines suspenseful elements typical of the genre with strong performances from its ensemble, effectively showcasing the talent of its actors.

Outcast Lady is a drama film directed by Robert Z. Leonard and released on September 28, 1934. The screenplay was crafted by Michael Arlen, and it features a notable performance by Constance Bennett. Set in the United States, this film explores the complexities of its characters' lives amidst societal challenges.

Anne of Green Gables, a film based on the beloved novel, was directed by George Nicholls, Jr. Released in 1934, this adaptation features a notable cast including Helen Westley, Ann Miller, and Bonita Granville. Produced by RKO Pictures, the film captures the charm of the original story, bringing to life the adventures of Anne Shirley in a vibrant and endearing manner.

Raula Pai Gaya is a 2012 Indian film that features a diverse cast, including Binnu Dhillon, Ravinder Grewal, Jaswinder Bhalla, B. N. Sharma, and Surbhi Jyoti. Released on August 31, 2012, this lively production showcases the talents of these actors, contributing to the film's engaging narrative.

I fuorilegge del matrimonio is a notable Italian comedy film released on January 1, 1963. The film, co-directed by Valentino Orsini, Vittorio Taviani, and Paolo Taviani, features an impressive cast, including Ugo Tognazzi, Scilla Gabel, Marina Malfatti, Annie Girardot, and Romolo Valli. 

In this production, the witty screenplay penned by Valentino Orsini complements the comedic talents of its cast, making it a memorable entry in the genre. Set against the vibrant backdrop of Italy, the film expertly combines humor with social commentary.

Dead or Alive, a Swiss drama film directed and co-written by Alain Tanner, was released on January 1, 1969. The film features a talented cast that includes Jean-Luc Bideau, Maya Simon, François Simon, and Francis Reusser, each contributing to the compelling narrative. Notably, this film was honored with the prestigious Golden Leopard award, highlighting its impact within the cinematic landscape.

Rauschende Melodien is a German musical film directed and written by Ernst Wilhelm Fiedler. Set against the vibrant backdrop of Vienna, the film features performances from Joseph Egger and Jarmila Kšírová, contributing to its charm and allure. With its captivating narrative and memorable music, this production reflects the rich cultural atmosphere of its location.

In the comedy film Paul Blart: Mall Cop 2, directed by Andy Fickman, Kevin James and Nick Bakay contributed to the screenplay. This sequel, which showcases the adventures of the titular character, was released in the United States on April 9, 2015. Notable cast members include Daniella Alonso and Paula Trickey. Produced by Happy Madison Productions, the film continues to explore themes of humor and heroism in the mall security setting.

Salt of the Earth: Palestinian Christians in the Northern West Bank is a documentary film that was released on January 1, 2004. This poignant work explores the lives and challenges faced by Palestinian Christians living in the Northern West Bank, providing a vital perspective on the complexities of identity and faith in a turbulent region.

sent: Seopyeonje, a poignant drama film released in 1993, showcases the talents of acclaimed director Im Kwon-taek. The screenplay is a collaborative effort by Yi Chong-jun and Kim Myung-gon, both of whom also appear in the cast. Set against the backdrop of South Korea, the film delves into themes of traditional music and familial bonds. Its rich narrative and emotional depth have solidified its status as a significant work in South Korean cinema.

Pierre of the Plains is a 1942 American drama film directed by George B. Seitz and featuring a screenplay by Lawrence Kimble. Starring John Carroll, this film delves into themes that resonate with audiences even today. Having been released in the early part of the year, it captures the spirit of its time while still feeling relevant.

Twins from Texas is a comedy film that showcases the creativity of both Italian and Spanish cinema, directed by Stefano Vanzina. The screenplay was crafted by Santos Alcocer Bádenas and Renzo Tarabusi, which contributed to its unique storytelling style. 

Featuring a talented cast, the film stars Umberto Raho, Raimondo Vianello, and Diana Lorys, who deliver engaging performances that enhance the lighthearted narrative. This delightful blend of humor and drama reflects the charm of European filmmaking during the era.

Pleasure Before Business is a film directed by Frank R. Strayer and features Virginia Brown Faire in a prominent role. This American production showcases Strayer's directorial style while highlighting Faire's performance, adding depth to the storyline.

Saroja, a comedy-drama directed and written by Venkat Prabhu, showcases a vibrant narrative set in Hyderabad. Released on September 5, 2008, this Indian film features Shiva in a prominent role, contributing to its engaging storyline. The blend of humor and drama in this work highlights the diverse cinematic landscape of India.

Kazimierz Kutz directed the acclaimed war film Salt of the Black Earth, which was released on March 6, 1970. This Polish production features a notable cast, including Gustaw Holoubek, Olgierd Łukaszewicz, and Jan Englert. 

Filming took place in various locations, including Bytom, Ruda Śląska, Świętochłowice, and Katowice, all contributing to the film's authentic portrayal of its setting. Not only recognized for its artistic merits, Salt of the Black Earth was also nominated for the International Submission to the Academy Awards, highlighting its significance in cinema.

triples.obj: International Submission to the Academy Awards

sent: I giganti di Roma is an adventure film directed by Antonio Margheriti. The film features Goffredo Unger in a prominent role, showcasing his talent alongside a screenplay written by Ernesto Gastaldi. Set in ancient Rome, this cinematic piece captures the essence of a grand adventure, inviting viewers into a world of epic storytelling.

Las 13 rosas is a gripping drama film directed by Emilio Martínez-Lázaro that explores the poignant themes surrounding the Spanish Civil War. Released in 2007, this Spanish movie features a talented cast, including Bárbara Lennie, Marta Etura, and Miren Ibarguren, all of whom deliver compelling performances that bring the historical narrative to life. 

The screenplay for this powerful film was penned by Ignacio Martínez de Pisón, ensuring a thoughtful depiction of the events that unfold. Notably, Secundino de la Rosa Márquez and Jasmine Trinca also play key roles, contributing to the film's emotional depth.

Salto is a Polish drama film directed by Tadeusz Konwicki, which premiered on June 11, 1965. Featuring a notable performance by Zbigniew Cybulski, this film explores deep themes characteristic of Konwicki's work. The emotional depth and rich storytelling have made it a significant piece in Polish cinema.

Tales of Erotica, directed and written by Piero Regnoli, is a notable comedy film from Italy that was released in January 1973. The story features a talented cast that includes Femi Benussi, Luigi Montini, Orchidea De Santis, Rosemarie Lindt, and Tony Kendall, all of whom contribute to the film's playful humor and engaging narrative.

Salute, an Australian film directed by Matt Norman, features a notable performance by John Carlos. The intriguing story brought to life by this talented cast highlights the distinct storytelling style characteristic of Australian cinema.

X-Men: Apocalypse, directed by Bryan Singer, was released on May 18, 2016. This apocalyptic and superhero film features Jennifer Lawrence among its cast members, showcasing her as one of the key characters. The narrative takes place in East Berlin and is brought to life by the collaboration of screenwriters Michael Dougherty and Bryan Singer, under the production of TSG Entertainment.

Michael Brandt serves as both the director and screenwriter of The Double, a gripping drama film that explores complex themes of identity and betrayal. Stana Katic delivers a compelling performance in this thought-provoking narrative. The film's intricate plot and strong character development highlight Brandt's adept storytelling abilities.

Days of Inspector Ambrosio, a crime film directed by Sergio Corbucci, was released on October 21, 1988. This Italian movie features a notable cast, including Ugo Tognazzi, Amanda Sandrelli, Carla Gravina, and Pupella Maggio. 

With Corbucci also serving as the screenwriter, the film weaves an engaging narrative that showcases the talents of its ensemble cast, which also includes Sal Borgese. Set against the backdrop of Italy, this film remains a testament to Corbucci's skill in crafting compelling crime stories.

Just Behind the Door, directed by Mansur Madavi, is a poignant Austrian drama film released on January 1, 1984. Notably, this film was nominated for the International Submission to the Academy Awards, highlighting its cultural significance and artistic merit.

sent: Salute John Citizen is a drama film directed by Maurice Elvey, released in the United Kingdom on January 1, 1942. Featuring Edward Rigby in the cast, this British film explores themes pertinent to its era, making it a notable entry in early 20th-century cinema.

Villa for Sale, directed by Géza von Cziffra, is a Hungarian film that premiered on April 10, 1935. The engaging screenplay, crafted by László Vadnay, features performances by actors Sándor Pethes and Lili Berky, adding depth to this classic narrative. This charming film showcases the rich cinematic tradition of Hungary during the early 20th century.

Lady in the Spa, directed by Edmund Hahn, is a silent film that debuted on August 20, 1929. This intriguing movie features performances from Robert Garrison, Helen Münchhofen, and Albert Paulig, who all contribute to its engaging narrative. Set against a backdrop that highlights the artistic style of its time, the film captures the essence of silent storytelling through its captivating visuals and exceptional performances.

Salute the Toff is a British film directed by Maclean Rogers and released on January 1, 1952. The movie features a talented cast including John Bentley, Valentine Dyall, and Carol Marsh. The screenplay was penned by John Creasey, adding to the film's intriguing narrative.

Roberto Faenza directed the poignant film I giorni dell'abbandono, which explores themes of love and abandonment. The cast features notable performances from Margherita Buy and Fausto Maria Sciarappa, who bring depth to their characters in this emotionally charged story. Their contributions greatly enhance the film's exploration of personal turmoil and resilience.

Helmut Käutner directed the drama film Sky without stars, showcasing his remarkable talent both behind the camera and in front of it, as he also plays a role in the film. This German production features a strong performance by Siegfried Lowitz alongside Gustav Knuth, creating a compelling narrative that resonates with audiences. Käutner's dual contribution as director and screenwriter adds a unique depth to this cinematic work.

Salute to the Marines, directed by S. Sylvan Simon and released in 1943, is an American film that delves into the themes of the Pacific War during World War II. As a propaganda and war film, it features Wallace Beery, who plays a significant role in portraying the struggles and valor of the Marines in this pivotal conflict. The film was produced during a time when the United States was heavily involved in the war, making its themes particularly resonant with contemporary audiences.

Days of Harvest, a drama film directed by Marco Righi, was released on January 1, 2010. Set in Italy, this poignant story features Lavinia Longhi in a prominent role, contributing to its emotional depth. The film explores themes that resonate deeply with its audience, showcasing the talent of its director and cast.

Malambo, directed by Milan Dor, features a talented cast including Klaus Rohrmoser and Oliver Stern. Produced by Dor Film, this Brazilian film showcases a compelling narrative that captivates viewers.

Directed by Lawrence Gough, the horror film Salvage was released in the United Kingdom on January 1, 2009. Featuring a talented cast that includes Linzey Cocker, Neve McIntosh, and Shaun Dooley, this British horror story explores unsettling themes that resonate with fans of the genre.

Directed by H. C. Potter, The Time of Your Life is a drama film set in the vibrant backdrop of San Francisco. The narrative features a talented cast, including Broderick Crawford, Wayne Morris, James Cagney, and Tom Powers, who bring to life the story based on the play of the same name. This American film captures the essence of its source material while exploring the intricacies of human relationships against the city's unique atmosphere.

Renato Castellani directed the drama film A Pistol Shot, showcasing a powerful narrative that reflects on complex themes. The movie was produced by Lux Film and features a talented cast, including Fosco Giachetti in a prominent role. Multiple distinguished screenwriters contributed to its script, including Castellani himself, along with Alberto Moravia, Mario Bonfantini, and Corrado Pavolini, each adding their unique voice to the storytelling. This collaboration resulted in a compelling cinematic experience deeply rooted in Italian film tradition.

Directed by Jack Hively, the film Anne of Windy Poplars was produced by RKO Pictures and released on January 1, 1940. This American production features Anne Shirley in a prominent role, bringing to life the beloved character in a charming adaptation. Set in the picturesque backdrop of the United States, it captures the spirit of the early 20th century with warmth and nostalgia.
Adrian Brunel directed the British propaganda film Salvage with a Smile. This production, originating from the United Kingdom, aimed to promote positive messages during its release.

I Giovani Tigri is a drama film directed by Antonio Leonviola that premiered in Italy in January 1968. The film features notable performances from actors such as Helmut Berger, Ray Lovelock, and Luca De Filippo. Set against a backdrop of intense emotional themes, this Italian production explores deep human connections and conflicts.

Söndrige Sondre is a Swedish film released on January 1, 2004. Both the direction and screenplay for the film were crafted by Daniel Halasz, showcasing his talents behind the camera and in the writer's room.

Directed by Beth B, the parody film Salvation! was released on January 1, 1987. This American production features Stephen McHattie in one of its key roles, contributing to its unique take on its subjects.

Grosse Pointe Blank is a notable American film directed by George Armitage, blending elements of dark comedy and action. The film, which tackles themes related to terrorism, features an impressive cast, including Hank Azaria, Dan Aykroyd, Alan Arkin, and Minnie Driver. Additionally, John Cusack not only stars in the lead role but also contributed to the screenplay alongside Steve Pink and Tom Jankiewicz. With its unique blend of humor and serious subject matter, this film has earned a special place in the hearts of many viewers.

Salvation, directed by Paul Cox, is an Australian film that features the talented actress Wendy Hughes. This poignant story showcases the unique vision of its director while highlighting the compelling performance by Hughes, making it a notable entry in Australian cinema.

Excellent Cadavers is a drama film directed by Ricky Tognazzi, which was produced by HBO and released on January 1, 1999. The cast includes notable actors such as Chazz Palminteri, F. Murray Abraham, Anna Galiena, and Tognazzi himself. This film explores deep themes, weaving a compelling narrative through the performances of its talented ensemble.

Listen Up Philip, a comedy-drama directed and written by Alex Ross Perry, was released on January 20, 2014. Set against the backdrop of New York City, the film explores the life of an aspiring writer, played by Jason Schwartzman, as he navigates the complexities of artistic ambition and personal relationships.

The film features a talented cast, including Elisabeth Moss, Eric Bogosian, Krysten Ritter, and Jonathan Pryce, all of whom bring depth to their characters. The narrative unfolds in the vibrant atmosphere of New York City, making the city almost a character in its own right.

Directed by James Cruze, Salvation Nell is a captivating drama film that showcases the talents of Helen Chandler and Ralph Graves in leading roles. Released in the United States on January 1, 1931, this film was crafted by screenwriter Edward Sheldon, weaving a story that resonates even today. Its rich narrative and emotional depth remain notable hallmarks of early 20th-century cinema.

Clarissa, a romance film released on September 8, 1941, showcases the talents of several prominent actors, including Klaus Pohl, Olga Engl, and Gustav Diessl. Directed by Gerhard Lamprecht and penned by Thea von Harbou, this German production explores themes of love and relationships against the backdrop of its historical context.

Featuring an ensemble cast that also includes Sybille Schmitz and Gustav Fröhlich, the film highlights the emotional depth typical of its genre. Through its engaging narrative and strong performances, Clarissa remains a notable entry in the canon of German cinema from the early 1940s.

The 39 Steps, directed by Ralph Thomas, is a captivating mystery film set in the bustling city of London. This British film not only draws inspiration from John Buchan's novel The Thirty-nine Steps but also incorporates elements of the spy genre. 

With a compelling cast featuring Taina Elg and Brenda De Banzie, the production by the Rank Organisation brings a thrilling narrative to life. The combination of suspense and intrigue makes it a notable adaptation that appeals to fans of both literature and cinema.

Directed and written by Joaquín Luis Romero Hernández Marchent, The Seven from Texas is an intriguing Italian film that captivates audiences with its unique blend of storytelling and style. This cinematic work, showcasing the director's distinctive approach, has garnered attention for its memorable characters and engaging plot.

Salvation Nell is a silent drama film directed by Kenneth Webb and written by Edward Sheldon. Released on January 1, 1921, this American production features Pauline Starke in a prominent role. The film is notable for its exploration of dramatic themes within the constraints of silent cinema.

Taras Bulba, directed by Joseph N. Ermolieff, is a silent film released in Germany in January 1924. This film is an adaptation of the literary work Taras Bulba, which contributes to its distinct narrative style. The cast features talent such as Clementine Plessner, Helena Makowska, and Oskar Marion, bringing the characters from the book to life on screen. Isaak Ezrovitch Douvan and Oscar Marion also deliver compelling performances in this cinematic interpretation, enhancing the storytelling experience.

Salve, a drama film directed and written by Alireza Davood Nejad, was released in Iran on January 1, 2011. The film features a talented cast, including Tannaz Tabatabaei and Reza Davood-Nejad, who bring the poignant story to life. As a reflective piece from Iran, it explores deep emotional themes, resonating with audiences through its compelling narrative and powerful performances.

I sette fratelli Cervi, a poignant drama film directed by Gianni Puccini, was released on January 1, 1968. The screenplay, crafted by renowned writer Cesare Zavattini, tells a powerful story that resonates with themes of family and resistance. The film features a notable cast, including Gian Maria Volonté and Lisa Gastoni, both of whom deliver memorable performances. Hailing from Italy, this cinematic work remains significant in the landscape of historical dramas.

The Hunchback of Notre Dame, directed by Wallace Worsley, is a classic silent romance film produced by Universal Pictures. This adaptation, which draws from Victor Hugo's novel, features a notable cast including Brandon Hurst, Ernest Torrence, and Patsy Ruth Miller. Set in the backdrop of medieval Paris, it beautifully combines elements of romance and drama, showcasing the intricate relationships between its characters amid the iconic architecture of Notre Dame. As one of the early cinematic interpretations of Hugo's work, it retains a significant place in film history, particularly within the genres of silent and romantic cinema.

Diary of a Coquette, a silent drama film directed by Constantin J. David, was released in Germany on March 22, 1929. The film features a notable cast, including Mary Kid, Paul Henckels, and Mathias Wieman, with supporting performances by Ernst Stahl-Nachbaur and Ida Wüst. The screenplay was crafted by Hans Wilhelm and Henry Koster, adding depth to this intriguing exploration of themes within the genre.

Released on January 1, 1951, I Sette nani alla riscossa is an Italian comedy film directed and written by Paolo William Tamburella. The film features notable performances from Guido Celano, Roberto Risso, and Ave Ninchi, among others. Set in Italy, this lighthearted film presents a fresh take on classic themes of humor and adventure.

Salve Geral, directed by Sérgio Rezende, is a Brazilian crime film that was released on October 2, 2009. The story unfolds in São Paulo and features Andréa Beltrão in a prominent role, immersing viewers in a gripping narrative that reflects the complexities of urban life.

The Dirties, directed by Matt Johnson, is a unique blend of drama and comedy that premiered on January 1, 2013. This Canadian film cleverly intertwines humor with serious themes, offering a thought-provoking yet entertaining experience. With its innovative approach, it stands out in the landscape of indie cinema.

Salviamo la montagna muore is a 1952 Italian film directed by Piero Nelli. This notable work showcases Nelli's unique storytelling capabilities, set against the backdrop of Italy. Released on January 1, 1952, it has since become a part of the country's cinematic heritage.

Queen Kelly is a silent drama film that showcases the talents of Erich von Stroheim, who not only directed the film but also contributed as a screenwriter alongside Paul L. Stein, Delmer Daves, and Edmund Goulding. Set in the United States, this intriguing piece features performances by notable cast members such as Sylvia Ashton and Sidney Bracey. The film is a testament to the craftsmanship of its era, blending compelling storytelling with the unique characteristics of silent cinema.

Directed by Ralph Habib, The Black Chapel is a 1959 drama film set against the backdrop of Rome. This compelling story features notable performances by Peter van Eyck and Werner Peters, both of whom bring depth to their roles. The film captures the essence of its Roman setting, making it an intriguing piece of cinema from that era.

Sorrowful Jones, a 1949 comedy film directed by Sidney Lanfield, features the talented Bob Hope in the leading role. Set against a backdrop of gambling, this American production combines humor with the intricacies of wagering, making it a notable entry in the genre. The film offers a lighthearted take on its main subject, showcasing the adventures and misfortunes that come with betting and the pursuit of fortune.

Heinz Paul takes the helm as both director and screenwriter of The False Prince, a notable entry in the silent film genre. The film features performances by Mary Kid and Josefine Dora, contributing to its engaging narrative. This Brazilian film utilizes its unique storytelling approach to explore themes that resonate with audiences.

Directed and written by Errol Morris, The Fog of War is a compelling documentary film that delves into the complexities of the Vietnam War. This biographical work not only explores the intricacies of war but also offers profound insights into the human condition. Released on January 1, 2003, it went on to receive critical acclaim, ultimately winning the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature Film.

Set against the backdrop of historical events, this American film serves as a poignant reflection on the lessons learned from a tumultuous period in history. The documentary’s release was followed by a limited re-release on September 30, 2004, further solidifying its status as a significant cinematic achievement in the genre of war and biography.

triples.obj: Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature Film

sent: Released on January 1, 1977, Mr. Rossi's Dreams is an adventure film directed by Bruno Bozzetto, who also co-wrote the screenplay alongside Maurizio Nichetti and Guido Manuli. This Italian production features Giuseppe Rinaldi among its cast, bringing the delightful and surreal dreams of Mr. Rossi to life.

Sorry, Haters is a drama film directed and written by Jeff Stanzler. Released in January 2005, the production takes place in the vibrant setting of New York City. The film features a talented cast, including Élodie Bouchez, Sandra Oh, Aasif Mandvi, and Robin Wright, who bring the story to life with their exceptional performances. Set in the United States, this gripping narrative explores complex themes against the backdrop of urban life.

Father Voss is a silent film directed by Max Mack, known for its evocative storytelling and rich character exploration. The screenplay was crafted by Robert Liebmann, who skillfully brought the narrative to life. Hermann Picha's performance adds depth to the film, showcasing the talents of early cinema. This German production exemplifies the artistry of the silent film era, capturing the audience without the need for spoken dialogue.

Directed by Dia Sokol Savage, Sorry, Thanks is a comedic film that comes from the United States. The movie features Wiley Wiggins as one of its cast members, contributing to the film's unique blend of humor and relatable storytelling. Audiences can expect a delightful exploration of life's quirks through its engaging narrative.

Directed by Irwin Winkler, the mystery film The Net was released on September 28, 1995. This gripping thriller explores themes of privacy and identity in the digital age, showcasing a tense narrative that keeps audiences on the edge of their seats.

I sogni muoiono all'alba is an Italian film directed by both Indro Montanelli and Enrico Gras. Released in January 1961, this poignant movie features the talented Lea Massari in its cast, adding depth to its narrative. The collaboration between the directors and the performances of the cast contribute to the film's lasting impact.

Sorry is a Japanese film directed by Shin Togashi and penned by Kota Yamada. This intriguing movie showcases the unique storytelling style typical of Japanese cinema, weaving together emotional depth and compelling narratives.

The Great Opportunity, a German film directed by Lorand von Kabdebo, was released on July 1, 1925. This silent era production features a notable cast that includes Lia Eibenschütz, Harry Nestor, and Colette Brettel, alongside Rudolf Lettinger and Kurt Vespermann. The screenplay was crafted by Henry Koster, contributing to the film's narrative depth during its time.

A három testör Afrikában is a Hungarian film directed by István Bujtor, released in January 1996. This adventure comedy is based on the classic tale of The Three Musketeers, but with a unique twist set against the backdrop of Africa. Through its engaging storyline, the film brings a fresh perspective to the beloved characters.

Gianni Puccini directed the Italian film I soldi, which features a talented cast including Agnès Spaak, Sylva Koscina, Tomas Milian, and Barbara Steele. Known for its intriguing plot and strong performances, this movie showcases the diverse talents of its ensemble. The contributions of each actor play a significant role in bringing the story to life.

Sorry Enaku Kalyanamayidichu is an Indian erotic film directed by Sagar, which was released on December 23, 2005. The film features performances from actors Livingston, Sriman, and Swarnamalya, contributing to its intriguing narrative.

I Lost My Heart in Heidelberg is a charming musical and romance film that transports viewers to the picturesque city of Heidelberg, Germany. Directed by Ernst Neubach, this German production features a talented cast, including Adrian Hoven, Herbert Hübner, and Reinhard Kolldehoff, who bring the story to life with their performances. The screenplay, penned by Gustav Kampendonk, weaves together themes of love and music, making it a delightful watch for fans of the genre.

sent: Triple Cross is a film directed by Terence Young that portrays the complexities of espionage during World War II. Featuring Harry Meyen in a prominent role, this British film delves into the thrilling and often dangerous world of double agents and their impact on the war efforts. The narrative provides a gripping look at loyalty and betrayal amid the backdrop of one of history's most significant conflicts.

Directed by Enrico Lando, I soliti idioti: Il film is a comedic exploration set in Rome. The screenplay, crafted by Fabrizio Biggio, showcases the hilarity and chaos of everyday life in the Italian capital, presenting a blend of urban humor and relatable absurdities.

Sorry Bhai!, directed by Onir, is an Indian film that features a talented cast, including Boman Irani, Shabana Azmi, and Chitrangada Singh. Released on January 1, 2008, this engaging story explores complex relationships with a blend of humor and emotion, showcasing the unique dynamics within a family.

In Heaven is a drama film directed by Michael Bindlechner, which was released on January 1, 1999. This poignant story features a talented cast, including Xaver Hutter and Sylvie Testud. The screenplay was penned by Isabel Dawn, adding depth to the narrative that intertwines love and life's challenges.
Directed by Pramod Chakravorty, the Indian film 12 O'Clock was released on January 1, 1958. This intriguing work is a notable entry in Indian cinema from that era.

Treasure Island, directed by Byron Haskin, premiered on July 19, 1950, and later had its wide release on November 27 of the same year. This film, based on the classic literary work by Robert Louis Stevenson, features memorable characters such as Jim Hawkins, Billy Bones, and the infamous Long John Silver, brought to life by the impressive performances of Howard Douglas and Basil Sydney.

Soulboy, directed by Shimmy Marcus, debuted on January 1, 2010. Featuring Felicity Jones in its cast, this British film explores themes of youth and music set against the backdrop of the Northern Soul scene.

A Fighting Man, a gripping drama and boxing film directed and written by Damian Lee, showcases the struggles of its protagonist against the backdrop of Toronto. Released on January 1, 2014, this Canadian production delves into themes of resilience and redemption within the boxing world. The film effectively captures the essence of its genre while highlighting the vibrant atmosphere of its filming location.

Joe e suo nonno is a musical film from Italy that blends elements of blues and rock music. Released on January 1, 1992, this charming story is set in the vibrant city of Naples.

Souli is a drama film directed by Alexander Abela that was released on January 1, 2004. This captivating work originates from both France and the United Kingdom, showcasing a poignant narrative that resonates with audiences.

Der Herrscher, a German drama film directed by Veit Harlan, features a notable cast that includes Emil Jannings, Rudolf Klein-Rogge, and Käthe Haack. The screenplay was penned by Curt Johannes Braun, adding depth to the film's compelling story. Additionally, Marianne Hoppe and Hilde Körber deliver memorable performances that contribute to the film's dramatic narrative.

Souls Protest is a disaster film from North Korea that was released on January 1, 2000. This intriguing work explores themes of survival and resilience in the face of catastrophic events, offering viewers a unique perspective typical of the region's cinematic approach.

Joe the Red, a comedy film directed by Raffaello Matarazzo, features a talented cast including Ada Dondini, María Denis, and Ugo Sasso. Released on January 1, 1936, this entertaining cinematic piece showcases the creative writing of Guglielmo Giannini. The film stands out as a notable example of Brazilian cinema from the 1930s, blending humor with engaging performances.

Before the Postman, directed by Mario Bonnard, is a notable Italian film released in 1942. Set against the backdrop of Rome, this work features performances from actors Enrico Luzi and Wanda Capodaglio, both of whom contribute to the film's charm. The screenplay is co-written by Bonnard himself, alongside the celebrated Federico Fellini, showcasing a collaboration between two prominent figures in Italian cinema. Produced by Cines, the film reflects the artistry and storytelling prevalent in Italy during that era.

Sound Off is a comedy film directed by Richard Quine and features a screenplay by Blake Edwards. The United States served as the backdrop for this lively production, which showcases the talents of cast member Mickey Rooney. With its blend of humor and engaging performances, this film remains a notable addition to the American comedy genre.

Directed by Richard Lester, How I Won the War is a 1967 comedy film set during World War II. Based on a novel and featuring a screenplay written by Patrick Ryan, this satirical take on wartime experiences showcases notable performances from Alexander Knox and Robert Hardy. The film cleverly blends humor with its historical subject matter, offering a unique perspective on the absurdities of war.

A Man Betrayed is a 1936 drama film directed by John H. Auer, showcasing a talented cast that includes Carleton Young, John Wray, and Edwin Maxwell. Set in the United States, the film explores themes of betrayal and trust within a gripping narrative. The performances by the cast members contribute significantly to the film's emotional depth and resonance.

Released on April 5, 2013, Sound Thoma is an Indian comedy film directed by Vyshakh. The screenplay was crafted by Benny P. Nayarambalam, who infused the film with humor and wit.

The cast features notable performances from Dileep, who plays the main character Gopalakrishnan P Pillai, alongside Namitha Pramod and veteran actor Nedumudi Venu. This engaging film showcases the richness of Indian comedy and has been well-received by audiences.

Aa Gaye Munde U.K. De is a lighthearted comedy film directed by Manmohan Singh that showcases the vibrant dynamics of Indian culture. The film features a talented ensemble cast, including Om Puri, Jimmy Shergill, Gurpreet Ghuggi, Binnu Dhillon, and Gugu Gill, each adding their unique flair to the story. Set against the backdrop of India, this entertaining flick provides a humorous take on life and relationships.

Sound an Alarm is a documentary film from the United Kingdom that was released on January 1, 1962. This British documentary delves into themes that resonate deeply with society, offering a thought-provoking perspective on its subject matter.

Michael Winterbottom's A Cock and Bull Story features an impressive cast, including notable performances from Shirley Henderson and Keeley Hawes. This British film is well-regarded for its unique storytelling approach, blending elements of comedy and drama.

Johanna Enlists, directed by William Desmond Taylor, features the renowned actress Mary Pickford in its cast. The screenplay of this film was penned by Frances Marion, known for her exceptional storytelling and character development.

Beloved Augustin is a historical film directed by E. W. Emo. Set against the backdrop of early 20th-century Austria, the movie features Richard Eybner in a significant role, bringing depth to its compelling narrative. This Austrian production captures a poignant moment in history through its vivid storytelling and strong performances.

Sound and Fury, directed by Josh Aronson, is a compelling documentary that explores the complexities of the Deaf community and the choices families face regarding cochlear implants. Released in 2000, this film earned a nomination for the Independent Spirit Award for Best Documentary Feature, highlighting its significant impact and critical acclaim in the realm of independent cinema.

sent: A Crime, directed by Manuel Pradal, is a gripping drama and crime film that delves into the complexities of morality and justice. The film showcases strong performances, particularly from cast members Kim Director and Lily Rabe, who bring depth to their roles and contribute to the narrative's tension.

Aadama Jaichomada is a 2014 Indian sport film directed by Badri, featuring a screenplay by Shiva. Central to the narrative is the theme of gambling, which is explored through the experiences of the characters, including a notable performance by cast member Karunakaran. The film offers insight into the world of competitive games and the risks associated with betting in sports.

Sound of Boot, a gripping thriller film directed by Shaji Kailas, features notable performances by Suresh Gopi and Bala. Released on January 1, 2008, this Indian film captivates audiences with its intense narrative and engaging characters. The interplay between the cast adds a dynamic layer to the story, making it a standout entry in the thriller genre.

Miracle in Cell No. 7, a poignant South Korean film directed and written by Lee Hwan-kyung, seamlessly blends elements of drama and the prison genre. Set against the backdrop of Seoul and Daejeon, this emotional narrative features remarkable performances by cast members Jeong Jin-yeong and Park Shin-hye. The film tells a heartwarming story that resonates deeply with audiences, showcasing both humor and sorrow within the confines of a prison setting.

Aambala is an action comedy film directed by Sundar C, which was released in India on January 1, 2015. Featuring Vishal in the lead role, this lively film blends humor with thrilling action sequences, offering audiences an entertaining cinematic experience.

A Dangerous Man, directed by Keoni Waxman, is an action film that was released on January 1, 2009. Featuring a cast that includes Steven Seagal, Jesse Hutch, and Mike Dopud, this film delves into themes of justice and retribution. With its fast-paced action sequences, it showcases Seagal's signature fighting style, alongside compelling performances from the supporting actors.

The Diamond Queen is a silent film directed by Edward A. Kull, which was released on March 15, 1921. Set in the United States, this cinematic work features performances by Eileen Sedgwick and George Chesebro, both of whom played pivotal roles in bringing the story to life. This film represents a notable example of early American cinema and showcases the unique storytelling style of the silent film era.

Sound of Horror is a captivating film directed by José Antonio Nieves Conde. This Spanish production features notable performances by Antonio Casas and Lola Gaos, who bring depth to the chilling narrative. Set against a backdrop of suspense, the film showcases the unique contributions of its talented cast, making it a memorable entry in the genre.

Directed by Victor Tourjansky, the German drama film Salto Mortale was released on September 17, 1953. The story features an impressive cast, including Christine Kaufmann, Gert Fröbe, Margot Hielscher, and Karlheinz Böhm, all of whom bring depth to this compelling narrative. With a screenplay by Felix Lützkendorf, the film captures the emotional intensity typical of its genre, showcasing the talents of its ensemble in a captivating manner.

The Diamond Master, a silent film directed by Jack Nelson, was released in the United States on January 1, 1929. This classic features performances by Louise Lorraine and Hayden Stevenson, showcasing the talent of its cast amidst the cinematic techniques of the silent era. The film remains a notable example of American filmmaking from the late 1920s.

A Dirty Shame, directed by John Waters, showcases the eccentricities of Baltimore, which serves as its vibrant backdrop. This film features a distinctive cast, including notable appearances by Patty Hearst and Johnny Knoxville. Produced by John Wells Productions, it dives into the quirky world of sexual liberation and censorship, reflecting Waters' signature provocative style.

The Secret Four, an action-packed silent film directed by both Albert Russell and Perry N. Vekroff, features Eddie Polo in a leading role. Released on January 1, 1921, this American production is recognized for its thrilling adventure sequences that captivated audiences of the time. The screenplay, penned by Anthony Coldeway, contributes to the film's enduring appeal and historical significance within the genre.

Sound of My Voice, a film directed by Zal Batmanglij, immerses viewers in a captivating story set in Los Angeles. The cast includes notable performances from Brit Marling, Davenia McFadden, and Constance Wu, each bringing depth to this intriguing narrative. Through their compelling portrayals, the film explores themes of belief and truth in a thought-provoking manner.
